title: per-route-price-experiments-notes
body:
Quick scratchpad for per-route pricing experiments — messy, rough, intended for thinking out loud. Notes on assumptions, 3 scenarios, quick unit math, UX/levers.

Goals: find simple primitives we can expose to product teams that map to cost drivers and value: (1) per-token unit, (2) per-request base for short chats, (3) latency SLA premium, (4) reservation/commit discount, (5) embedding-only pricing variant.

Assumptions (rough):
- infra marginal cost: ~ $0.007 per 1k tokens served (mix of model types, batching, KV cache). This is our backend-avg for hosted multitenant. (NOTE: need to validate with infra team; rough from last month’s usage sample)
- target gross margin on hosted: 70% (startup PLG benchmark)
- retail markup factor target = cost / (1 - margin) => 0.007 / 0.3 = 0.0233 per 1k tokens -> round to $0.024/1k
- embed cost (infer-only): infra cost ~ $0.0008 per embedding; target price $0.004–$0.006 per embedding

Scenario A: Simple PAYG (single per-token meter)
- Price: $0.024 / 1k tokens (as calculated)
- Example: 100k tokens -> 100 * 0.024 = $2.40
- Pros: super simple, easy to compare to competitors
- Cons: noisy bills for chat apps with many short turns; hard to favor low-latency reserved users

Scenario B: Hybrid (request base + token)
- Base per request (to capture RPC overhead + tiny tail latency infra): $0.001 per request
- Token unit: $0.020 per 1k tokens (slightly cheaper because base captures overhead)
- Example: 200 small messages, avg 50 tokens each = 10k tokens
  - Base: 200 * 0.001 = $0.20
  - Tokens: 10 * 0.020 = $0.20
  - Total = $0.40 -> effective per-1k = $40 / 1000? (ignore, keep example)
- Use case fit: conversational apps with many short-turn messages

Scenario C: Route-level SLA & priority pricing
- Idea: allow product to pick per-route flags: default, reserved-low-latency, best-effort
- Add multiplier for reserved: +15% on price (or flat premium $X/mo). Or create per-route commit: reserve X QPS for route -> discount vs burst price.
- Example: default price $0.024/1k; reserved route price $0.020/1k but requires 1-month commit of $Y (compute how to size Y later)

Bundles / Tiers (quick sketches)
- Starter: $9/mo -> includes 250k tokens, overage at $0.030/1k
- Builder: $49/mo -> includes 2.5M tokens, overage $0.018/1k
- Scale: $499/mo -> includes 40M tokens, overage $0.012/1k + 1 reserved route slot
- Rationale: price-per-token declines with commitment; overage rates set to encourage higher tiering

Reserved capacity / Dedicated discounts
- If customer commits to dedicated pool (monthly commit), we can offer 35–50% off hosted PAYG per-token
- Simplified model: hosted PAYG $0.024/1k; Dedicated commit price $0.015/1k (40% off)
- Also offer latency SLA add-on: +$X per reserved GPU hour or +10–20% on unit price depending on target p99

Edge cases / knobs to ship quickly
- Free tier credits: 100k tokens first 30 days
- Burst credits: allow short bursts at no extra charge up to 2x committed QPS for 1 hour/month
- Per-route quotas: let customers set per-route caps to limit cost surprises
- Developer UX: show per-route burn in Console + estimate for next 30 days based on trailing 7-day rate

Unit math checks (back of envelope):
- Backend cost calc basis (illustrative): GPU hr cost = $6/hr (amortized infra + ops), tokens/sec throughput = 120 tokens/sec -> tokens/hr = 432k tokens
  - cost per token = 6 / 432k = $0.0000139 per token -> per 1k tokens = $0.0139 -> this is optimistic for efficient large models
  - add overhead (or higher model size) -> adjust to $0.007 per 1k as blended above
- LTV sensitivity: if avg cust uses 5M tokens/mo, at $0.020/1k revenue = 100 * 0.02 = $100/month revenue. CAC target? needs separate sheet.

Open questions / TODO
- Validate blended infra cost with infra SRE (ticket ID refs above)
- Test UX: when do we expose per-request base vs keep hidden? Flag on route default=false
- Experiment plan: A/B test Hybrid pricing on small cohort (10 customers) for 8 weeks; measure retention, units consumed, complaints about billing clarity
- Metrics to track: ARPU by route type, churn vs cost, overage frequency, switch rate to reserved

Notes-to-self: capture examples from existing customers (e.g., embed-heavy search product vs chat-first consumer app) and model cost flows separately. Also think about making a "route credit" concept: each route gets an included monthly credit convertible to token budget or CPU QPS for dedicated.

— end scratchpad —
